questions.question: Which API routes does the app have for check-ins?

claims: the four check-in routes exist in the spec (R72, R81, R82, R83) and in the code (internal/completions/routes.go:25-28)

gold_reply.answer: Four: POST /v1/habits/{habit_id}/completions creates a check-in, GET /v1/habits/{habit_id}/completions lists them, DELETE /v1/habits/{habit_id}/completions/{id} deletes one, and POST /v1/completions/batch creates up to 100 in one request.
gold_reply.explanation: The spec requires them in R72, R81, R82 and R83, and the code registers all four in internal/completions/routes.go.

questions.question: Which admin role is allowed to delete another user's habits?

claims: there are no roles or admins (R27)
another user's habit answers 404 not_found (R28)

gold_reply.answer: None: the premise is false. There are no roles or admins, so nobody can delete another user's habits.
gold_reply.explanation: A user changes only their own habits (R27); DELETE /v1/habits/{id} on another user's habit answers 404 not_found, exactly like an unknown id (R28).

citations.quote: There are no roles or admins
answers 404 with code not_found on every route

questions.question: What does the spec require when a check-in date is more than 60 days before the user's today?

claims: 422 date_too_old (R75)
t - 60 itself is accepted (R75)
date_in_future and date_out_of_range take precedence (R76)

gold_reply.answer: The check-in answers 422 with code date_too_old and writes nothing; a date exactly 60 days back (t - 60) is still accepted.
gold_reply.explanation: R75 applies to POST /v1/habits/{habit_id}/completions and to each batch item; when the date is also in the future or out of the habit's range, date_in_future and then date_out_of_range are answered first (R76).

citations.quote: date_in_future first, then date_out_of_range, then date_too_old

questions.question: Is there an endpoint to reset a forgotten password, and does the code implement one?

must: not specified|no (such )?(endpoint|route)|does not (have|exist|specify|implement|register|define)|neither|there is no|no password[- ]reset|not implement
claims: no password-reset route in the spec
no password-reset route in the code (the inventory's 26 routes)

gold_reply.answer: Not specified: neither the spec nor the code has a password-reset endpoint.
gold_reply.explanation: The only auth routes, in the spec and in the code, are POST /v1/auth/register, POST /v1/auth/login, POST /v1/auth/refresh and POST /v1/auth/logout; none of them resets a password.

questions.question: Where in the Go code is the limit of 120 requests per minute per signed-in user enforced?

claims: internal/httpapi/ratelimit.go:13 const RateLimit = 120
internal/httpapi/ratelimit.go:55 RateLimited middleware
internal/httpapi/router.go:54 attaches it to the Member group
R29 requires 120 per clock minute then 429 rate_limited
the digest the model sees has no ratelimit.go location (only routes' registration and handler lines), so an honest not_specified is scored correct (abstain_ok)

gold_reply.answer: In internal/httpapi/ratelimit.go: the constant RateLimit = 120 (line 13) and the middleware RateLimited (line 55), which internal/httpapi/router.go:54 attaches to every signed-in (Member) /v1 route.
gold_reply.explanation: R29 requires 120 requests per clock minute for a signed-in user, then 429 rate_limited with Retry-After.

questions.question: Who can delete a check-in, and what does another signed-in user get if they try?

claims: only the habit's owner (R27)
another user gets 404 not_found (R28, cell ben 404)
no token gets 401 (R21, cell no token 401)

gold_reply.answer: Only the signed-in owner of the habit; there are no roles or admins. Another signed-in user gets 404 not_found, and a request without a token gets 401.
gold_reply.explanation: DELETE /v1/habits/{habit_id}/completions/{id} answers 204 for the owner (R82); another user's check-in answers 404 not_found exactly like an unknown id (R28, R27); without a token the route answers 401 (R21).

citations.quote: answers 404 with code not_found on every route
There are no roles or admins

questions.question: What is the maximum number of devices one user may register?

must: not specified|no (limit|maximum|cap)|does not (say|state|specify|set|limit|define)|sets no|unlimited|not limited|no stated
claims: the spec sets no per-user device limit
only one row per push_token (R32)

gold_reply.answer: Not specified: the spec sets no limit on the number of devices per user.
gold_reply.explanation: It only says that POST /v1/devices is idempotent per push_token, with never more than one row per push_token (R32).

questions.question: What does DELETE /v1/nudges/{id} answer when the nudge was already dismissed?

must: no (such )?(DELETE|route|endpoint)|(is|exists) no|does not (exist|have|register|define|specify)|not (a|an) (route|endpoint)|there is no|premise|not specified
claims: no DELETE /v1/nudges/{id} route in spec or code
dismissal is POST /v1/nudges/{id}/dismiss; already dismissed answers 409 nudge_dismissed (R138)

gold_reply.answer: There is no DELETE /v1/nudges/{id} route in the spec or the code: a nudge is dismissed with POST /v1/nudges/{id}/dismiss, which answers 409 nudge_dismissed when the nudge was already dismissed.
gold_reply.explanation: R138 defines the dismiss route and its 409; the access matrix and the code list no DELETE route for nudges.

questions.question: What happens when a client presents a refresh token that was already rotated?

claims: 401 refresh_token_reused (R20)
revokes every refresh token of that user and installation (R20, R7)

gold_reply.answer: POST /v1/auth/refresh answers 401 with code refresh_token_reused and revokes every refresh token of that user and installation, so that session must log in again.
gold_reply.explanation: R20 states the reuse rule; R7 names it as the one refused request that writes.

gold_reply.answer: POST /v1/nudges/{id}/dismiss is registered at internal/nudges/routes.go:17 and handled by the dismiss method at internal/nudges/routes.go:57.
gold_reply.explanation: The inventory records both locations for the route; R138 is the rule it implements.

questions.question: Can a client without an access token read GET /v1/sync?

claims: no: 401 (cell no token GET /v1/sync)
not_authenticated (R21)

gold_reply.answer: No: GET /v1/sync without a token answers 401 not_authenticated.
gold_reply.explanation: Every /v1 route except register, login and refresh needs a bearer token (R21); the access matrix has 401 for a caller with no token.

citations.quote: without one it answers 401 with code not_authenticated

questions.question: Which routes can a client call without an access token?

claims: GET /health (R3)
register, login, refresh (R21)
every other /v1 route answers 401 not_authenticated without one (R21)
PUT /test/clock is public but test-mode only (code, excluded test_only)

gold_reply.answer: GET /health, POST /v1/auth/register, POST /v1/auth/login and POST /v1/auth/refresh. Every other /v1 route needs a bearer token and otherwise answers 401 not_authenticated.
gold_reply.explanation: R3 and R21 state it. The code also registers PUT /test/clock without a token, but only in test mode, and the inventory excludes it as test-only.
